database.existing_project_inspection: Read-only introspection of the fixed regphejnlvfpyokpniny Management API reported no existing public.profiles relation. No migration was applied remotely.
database.creation: First explicit save creates the user row; a GET never inserts one.
database.privacy: RLS enabled; anonymous access and browser delete denied. Authenticated SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE policies require auth.uid() = id, including the conflict-update path. No other profile fields or credentials are returned.

behavior: First and last names are editable and validated; only explicit Google given/family name fields seed an absent row.
A valid IANA timezone is saved with the names. The saved preference overrides the browser timezone, including DST. Absent preferences and anonymous viewers use the browser timezone.
A shared hydration-safe time component displays an initial placeholder rather than server-timezone text. It preserves missing/invalid values and a real recorded epoch zero.

Assessment cards/queues/history, run status/timelines/history, chat dates and research protocol timestamps use the preference. Real-world date filters use calendar days in the display timezone, including 23/25-hour DST days.
Original timestamps, scientific configurations, time axes/durations, raw JSON/provenance and CSV/JSON downloads retain their recorded representations.
The previously requested removal of Assessment <id> text from catalog cards is preserved; the record identity still drives links and React keys.

browser.design: Actual built Next page, private GET and server action use a fixed loopback Supabase/Auth/PostgREST transport backed by actual isolated PostgreSQL with the migration and real RLS. The JWTs and accounts are explicitly synthetic and never accepted by a real service.
covered: Names/timezone persist through save and reload; selected source timestamp instant preserved
Invalid input, forged caller identity and cross-origin action cause no DB changes
Storage failure is visible; retry restores values
Desktop 1365/mobile 390 in light/dark; header profile link and no horizontal overflow
Second user receives only their own profile

checks.react_review: Server mutation authenticates again and validates every field; owner identity comes from verified auth. Data returned is narrow, no shared server user state or service keys; profile fetches are aborted/generation-checked on auth changes. Stable list IDs, labels, loading/error feedback and native time elements remain.

limitations: Production migration, real Google provider round trip and save behind the production CDN are unverified.
Browser persistence uses synthetic identity/HTTP transport and actual local SQL, not a legitimate user session.
Other modules compile with the shared formatter, but every module page was not independently exercised in a browser.
Changing the profile in another browser tab/device is read on reload or sign-in, without new polling.

release.status: Not committed, pushed, merged or deployed.

preserved_failures: An early TypeScript build found a nullable header profile access; fixed before passing builds/browser tests.
Sandbox network restrictions prevented the initial local PostgreSQL/browser campaign; original failed reports remain in ignored artifact directories.
The original AWS-based schema guard encountered expired AWS credentials. A direct fixed-project read-only Supabase introspection completed; no AWS login or production change was needed.
